2609.24890.title: OSWorld-Pro: Process-based Evaluation for Computer Use Agents
2609.24890.paper_summary: Evaluation of Computer-Use Agents (CUAs) is often limited to the final deliverables they create (at the end of hundreds of steps) and assessed with functional verifiers, as seen in OSWorld. However, such evaluation of end-state performance lacks transparency into how and why agents fail in various tasks, obfuscating critical insight for subsequent improvement. For instance, agents that err during keyboard inputs would require a different mitigation strategy from those that fail to precisely provide click-based inputs on the graphical UI. We introduce OSWorld-Pro: a set of over 300 tasks containing over 2800 subgoals to enable the procedural evaluation of CUAs grounded in over 67,000 human annotations. We use robust human-aligned LLM-Judges to evaluate the fulfillment of OSWorld-Pro subgoals and thereby reveal the progress that models make throughout a series of sequentially dependent subgoals. Our findings reveal that OSWorld-Pro is challenging even for state-of-the-art LLMs, with top performers like Claude Opus 5 achieving only 75.7% vs. 83.4% on OSWorld. Furthermore, we identify critical process-focused failure modes of various models (e.g. subgoal-irrelevant actions and click-based mistakes) to provide insights to improve performance and efficiency of CUAs.
2609.24890.paper_summary_zh: 評估計算機使用代理（CUAs）通常僅限於它們創建的最終交付成果（在數百個步驟的結尾），並使用功能驗證器進行評估，如在 OSWorld 中所見。然而，這種對最終狀態性能的評估缺乏對代理在各種任務中失敗的方式和原因的透明度，掩蓋了後續改進所需的關鍵見解。例如，在鍵盤輸入過程中出錯的代理需要與那些在圖形用戶界面上無法精確提供基於點擊的輸入的代理不同的緩解策略。我們介紹了 OSWorld-Pro：一組包含超過 300 個任務和 2800 個子目標的集合，以便基於超過 67,000 個人類註釋進行 CUAs 的程序性評估。我們使用強大的與人類對齊的 LLM-Judges 來評估 OSWorld-Pro 子目標的實現，從而揭示模型在一系列依賴於序列的子目標中的進展。我們的研究結果顯示，OSWorld-Pro 對於最先進的 LLM 來說是具有挑戰性的，像 Claude Opus 5 這樣的頂尖表現者在 OSWorld 上的達成率僅為 75.7%，而在 OSWorld 上則為 83.4%。此外，我們識別了各種模型的關鍵過程導向失敗模式（例如，與子目標無關的行為和基於點擊的錯誤），以提供改進 CUAs 性能和效率的見解。
